bms_4168_08003570.name: bms_rtc_wait_synchro
bms_4168_08003570.summary: Wait for the RTC register-sync flag (RSF) with a 1000-tick timeout; returns 0 or 3
bms_4168_08003570.description: Waits until the RTC shadow registers are synchronised, the same job as HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro. param_1 is a handle whose first word is the RTC register base, so RTC_ICSR is at base+0x0C and RTC_CR at base+0x18. The routine clears ICSR bit 7 (INIT) on every call, then clears RSF (ICSR bit 5, a write-0-to-clear flag) and polls until hardware sets it again. Polling is timed against the counter returned by bms_get_ram_word_200006a0; more than 1000 ticks elapsed means timeout, the handle's status byte at +0x29 becomes 3 and the function returns 3. When CR bit 5 is set it is cleared for the wait and set again afterwards, on both the success and timeout paths.

params.name: handle
params.description: param_1; word 0 is the RTC register base, byte +0x29 receives the status code

returns.description: 0 when RSF was seen, 3 on timeout

bms_4168_08003570.notes: Bit names follow the ST RTC layout (ICSR.INIT, ICSR.RSF, CR.BYPSHAD); the code shows only the bit positions, so those labels are medium confidence. The 1000 limit is in counter ticks; whether a tick is 1 ms depends on the SysTick setup, which is not in this packet.

bms_4168_08003614.name: RTC_TAMP_IRQHandler
bms_4168_08003614.summary: RTC/TAMP vector: passes the pointer slot at 0x20005D00 to bms_4168_08002542
bms_4168_08003614.description: Vector handler for the RTC and tamper interrupt. It has no logic of its own: it passes the address of the RAM slot at 0x20005D00 to bms_4168_08002542 (not yet described) and returns. The same slot holds a pointer that bms_nibble_debounce_1s dereferences, so the interrupt most likely services the object that slot points to.
bms_4168_08003614.notes: Vector name from the STM32G0 IRQ table; the handler is entered only through the vector.

bms_4168_08003662.name: SysTick_Handler
bms_4168_08003662.summary: SysTick vector: calls bms_counter_accumulate to advance the 32-bit counter at 0x200006A0
bms_4168_08003662.description: Core SysTick exception handler. It calls bms_counter_accumulate (bms_4168_080021b4), which adds the step word at 0x20000698 into the 32-bit counter at 0x200006A0. That counter is the one bms_get_ram_word_200006a0 returns, and bms_rtc_wait_synchro uses it for its 1000-tick timeout. It is a separate time base from the TIM7-driven tick at 0x20000678.

bms_4168_0800367c.name: TIM7_LPTIM2_IRQHandler
bms_4168_0800367c.summary: TIM7 update vector: clear the flag, advance the 0x20000678 tick, count down two timers
bms_4168_0800367c.description: Runs on each TIM7 update. It tests a status word with bms_request_is_done, passing &TIM7, and if it is set clears it with bms_request_reset (writes 0xFFFFFFFE at offset 0x10). It then increments the 32-bit tick at 0x20000678, which bms_tick_get returns, and decrements the 16-bit countdowns at 0x2000067C and 0x2000067E toward zero. The 0x2000067E countdown is the one bms_timeout_arm_from_record loads, so those timeouts run at the TIM7 update rate.
bms_4168_0800367c.notes: The wave-1 summaries describe bms_request_is_done and bms_request_reset as request-block helpers, but this call passes &TIM7 and offset 0x10 is TIM7.SR in the timer layout, so the test is most likely SR bit 0 (UIF). Re-check those two helpers against that reading. The width of 0x2000067C is not shown here.

bms_4168_080036d0.name: USART3_4_5_6_LPUART1_IRQHandler
bms_4168_080036d0.summary: USART3 vector: on RXNE clear ORE and pass the byte to bms_4168_08007c10; on IDLE clear it
bms_4168_080036d0.description: Reads USART3.ISR. If RXNE (bit 5) is set it writes 8 to USART3.ICR, reads one byte from USART3.RDR and passes it to bms_4168_08007c10 (not yet described). The ICR write happens on every RXNE, not only after an overrun. Otherwise, if IDLE (bit 4) is set, it writes 0x10 to ICR to clear IDLE and returns. The handler only moves bytes and clears the two flags; frame assembly must be in bms_4168_08007c10.
bms_4168_080036d0.notes: ICR bit meanings (ORECF = bit 3, IDLECF = bit 4) follow the ST layout.

bms_4168_0800379c.name: bms_banded_offset_compute
bms_4168_0800379c.summary: Compute a 0-501 offset from banded tables on the u16 at +0x18 and the s16 at +0x08
bms_4168_0800379c.description: Starts from bms_udiv32(u16 at +0x06, 3) + 50. It compares the u16 at +0x18 with five ascending bounds (20, 50, 80, 95, 100) and adds 1, 5, 10, 50 or 125 for the first bound it does not exceed. The signed s16 at +0x08 adds a second term: 4 when it is 0 or below, 5, 6, 6 or 10 for the bands (0,15], (15,30], (30,45] and (45,60], and 100 at 60 or above. The sum is clamped to 501 (0x1F5). Both tables are constants in the function's own frame, so the result depends only on the three input fields.

params.name: ctx
params.description: param_1; reads u16 +0x06, s16 +0x08 and u16 +0x18

bms_4168_0800379c.notes: The packet gives no unit or quantity. The sole caller, bms_4168_0800e3bc, is outside it. The band bounds look like percentages (100 at the top), which is an inference.

bms_4168_08003868.name: bms_throughput_accumulate
bms_4168_08003868.summary: Integrate |sample| x 10 and return whole 3600-scaled units to add to a total
bms_4168_08003868.description: param_1 is a record: byte +0x00 is a step added to the sample counter at 0x20000603, byte +0x02 is an enable flag, and s16 +0x14 is a signed sample. When enabled it adds |sample| x 10 to the running total at 0x2000060C and adds the step to the counter. Once the counter reaches 10 it divides the total by counter x 3600 with bms_udiv32, keeps the remainder in 0x2000060C, resets the counter and returns the quotient added to param_2. Below 10 it returns param_2 unchanged and both accumulators keep running. When the enable flag is clear it zeroes the total and the counter.

params.name: rec
params.description: param_1; byte +0x00 step, byte +0x02 enable, s16 +0x14 sample

params.name: acc
params.description: param_2; value the whole units are added to

returns.description: param_2 plus any whole units flushed this call

bms_4168_08003868.notes: The 3600 divisor suggests a seconds-to-hours scale, so this is probably charge throughput in ampere-hours. The sample's unit and source are not in the packet.

bms_4168_080039e8.name: bms_logical_addr_map
bms_4168_080039e8.summary: Map a logical record number to a device address for mode 0 or 1; other modes pass through
bms_4168_080039e8.description: param_1 selects the mapping. Mode 0 divides (DAT_20001348 - param_2) by 5, multiplies the quotient by 0x1000, adds the remainder times 0x294 and DAT_2000134C, and folds results at or above 0x268000 by subtracting it and adding 0x10000. Mode 1 splits param_2 into a page part (param_2 >> 6, times 0x1000) and a slot part (param_2 & 0x3F, times 0x40), adds DAT_20001358, and folds results at or above 0x390000 by subtracting it and adding 0x280000. Any other mode returns param_1 unchanged. The windows and strides suggest a logical-to-physical translation into a remapped store, but the packet does not show that store.

params.name: mode
params.description: param_1; 0 or 1 select a mapping, other values are returned as they are

params.name: record
params.description: param_2; logical record number

bms_4168_080039e8.notes: The mode-0 remainder is read from the second return word of bms_udiv32 (the decompiler shows a 64-bit return), but the wave-1 summary says only the quotient is returned. This needs checking. Net effect of the folds: -0x258000 in mode 0 and -0x110000 in mode 1.

bms_4168_08003fcc.name: bms_fault_timers_step
bms_4168_08003fcc.summary: Advance the fault-timer accumulators by one step; return 1 when one passes its limit
bms_4168_08003fcc.description: param_1 is the elapsed time added to each active accumulator. It reads the BMS status object at DAT_2000002C (u16 at +0x124 status bits, s16 at +0x11A, u16 at +0x19C, bit 0 of the byte at +0x194) and the object from bms_u32_20000dec_addr (u16 at +0x04). Five accumulators run while their conditions hold and clear when they fail: 0x20000048 and 0x2000004C for the +0x19C count below 10 and below 20 (limits 60,480,000 and 120,960,000); 0x20000058 for the count below 3 (limit 3,600,000), where the 0x124 bits 1 and 2 and the s16 below -49 decide resets; 0x20000054 while 0x124 bits 1 and 2 are clear and the object value is 3000 or less (limit 30,000); and 0x20000050 while 0x124 bit 4 is set and bit 2 is clear (limit 6,000). An accumulator that passes its limit is clamped and makes the function return 1. The 0x2000005C timer runs only while bit 3 of the byte at *DAT_20000030 is set: it drives PA15 low through gpio_pa15_reset and returns 1 after 200, and this function never resets it.

params.name: elapsed
params.description: param_1; time added to every active accumulator this step

returns.description: 1 when a timer has expired, 0 otherwise

bms_4168_08003fcc.notes: The limits read as milliseconds if the step is 1 ms (3600000 is one hour); that is an inference. The fields at +0x124, +0x194 and +0x19C are not labelled in the packet.

bms_4168_080040e4.name: bms_index_debounce_step
bms_4168_080040e4.summary: Debounce a 0-7 index from bms_4168_08008f50 into the 1-based field at status +0x1A
bms_4168_080040e4.description: Samples an index with bms_4168_08008f50 (not described here). The status field at DAT_2000002C+0x1A holds the index plus one, so the routine compares the stored value minus one with the new sample. While the state byte at 0x20000021 is 1 and the sample differs, a sample of 8 or more is ignored, a sample below 8 is counted in 0x20000022, and the field is written only when that count reaches 2. In every other case (state not 1, or the sample equals the stored index) the field is written at once and the state is set to 1. A single noisy sample therefore cannot move the stored index.
bms_4168_080040e4.notes: The counter at 0x20000022 is not cleared when samples agree, so the two differing samples need not be consecutive. The index's source and meaning are not in the packet; a slot or cell index is an inference from the 0-7 limit. The BMS_4139 image has a different body at the same address (bms_4139_080040e4); the packet lists both, so check the family map.

bms_4139_080040e4.name: bms_profile_block_fill_4139
bms_4139_080040e4.summary: Fill the 4139 parameter block for profile id 0x20000016 (nine cases, default otherwise)
bms_4139_080040e4.description: Chooses one parameter set from the profile id at DAT_20000016: ids 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 each have their own values, and every other id (including 1) takes the default set. The set supplies a capacity-like constant (values 5100 to 19200), used directly and divided by 10 into DAT_2000001C+0x26, several 16-bit limits (values such as 255, 765, 800 and 1200), and smaller fields stored into the block returned by FUN_0800C0D0 at offsets 0x2C, 0x30, 0x34, 0x38, 0x3A, 0x3C, 0x3E, 0x74, 0x76 and 0x7D. It copies three 11-entry u16 tables from RAM into the block at +0x00, +0x16 and +0x5E, chosen by id group (0-4, 6-8, or other). Fixed bytes go to +0x80 to +0x8F; only +0x81 and +0x87 differ between the 6-8 group and the rest.
bms_4139_080040e4.notes: The values are constants from this code, not measurements, and the units of the capacity-like value and of the block are not in the packet. Sibling fills: bms_profile_block_fill_4168, bms_profile_table_fill_4130 and bms_profile_table_fill_4139, which have different record layouts.

bms_4168_08004128.name: bms_profile_block_fill_4168
bms_4168_08004128.summary: Fill the 4168 parameter block for profile id 0x20000026 (13 ids, default set otherwise)
bms_4168_08004128.description: Picks one of nine sets from the profile id at DAT_20000026: ids 4 and 12 share a set, 3 and 11 share one (differing only in the byte at +0x3E, 7 or 6), 2 and 10 share one (byte at +0x3E 8 or 2), and 9, 0, 8, 6, 5 and 7 each have their own; any other id takes the default. Each set supplies a capacity-like value (5100 to 19200, used directly and divided by 10 into DAT_2000002C+0x26), 16-bit limits and small fields at +0x2C, +0x34, +0x38, +0x3A, +0x3C, +0x3E, +0x74 and +0x7D of the block returned by FUN_0800CE5C. It copies three 11-entry u16 tables for the id group (0-4, 6-8, 9-10, 11-12, or other) into +0x00, +0x16 and +0x5E. Fixed bytes go to +0x80 to +0x8F; +0x81, +0x82, +0x83 and +0x87 differ between the 6-8 group and the rest.
bms_4168_08004128.notes: Same role as bms_profile_block_fill_4139 for the 4168 build, with a different id-to-set mapping and different fixed bytes. The meaning of the capacity-like value is not in the packet.

bms_4130_08004208.name: bms_profile_table_fill_4130
bms_4130_08004208.summary: Write the 4130 table of 12-byte limit records and set the thresholds for profile id 0x20000014
bms_4130_08004208.description: Fills 17 records through bms_record12_addr (FUN_0800BAE0). Fourteen of them (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 0x0C, 0x0F, 0x16, 0x18, 0x1D, 0x1F and 0x21) are fixed u16 pairs with u32 words of 4000 or 10000, while records 0x11, 0x2B and 0x30 are derived from the status block. The profile id at DAT_20000014 selects threshold values stored in the status block: +0x52 and +0x86/+0x88 for id 5 or other ids, and +0x6C/+0x70/+0x76 for groups (4-5), (3), (2), (0) and other. Record 0x11 copies +0x86 and +0x88, record 0x2B takes +0x6C and +0x6C-2, and record 0x30 takes -(+0x70) and 2-(+0x70). The routine only writes.
bms_4130_08004208.notes: The purpose of individual records is not stated in the packet. The 4000 and 10000 words are probably limits or durations, which is an inference. The 4139 counterpart is bms_profile_table_fill_4139, which writes its threshold to +0x192 rather than +0x52.

bms_4139_08004388.name: bms_profile_table_fill_4139
bms_4139_08004388.summary: Fill the 4139 record table and threshold bytes for profile id 0x20000014
bms_4139_08004388.description: Fills 18 records through bms_record12_addr for the 4139 build (its accessor is FUN_0800C0B0). Records 2 and 3 take 4000 as the second word for ids 6, 7 and 8 and 0x1004 otherwise; record 0x12 copies +0x86 and +0x88; records 0x2C and 0x31 are derived from the status block; the rest are fixed pairs with u32 words of 4000 or 10000. The profile id at DAT_20000014 sets +0x86 and +0x88 (0x35 and 0x30 for ids 5 to 8, 0x3A and 0x35 otherwise) and the threshold at +0x192 (0x17C for id 5, 400 otherwise), and sets +0x6C, +0x70 and +0x76 by group: (4-5), (3, 6, 8), (2, 7), (0) and other. Records 0x2C and 0x31 take +0x6C and -(+0x70) as in the 4130 table.
bms_4139_08004388.notes: Same structure as bms_profile_table_fill_4130 with different ids, record numbers and offsets. The purpose of individual records is not stated in the packet.

bms_4130_08004410.name: bms_remaining_time_4130
bms_4130_08004410.summary: Update the minutes-like estimate at status +0x128 with hold and hysteresis (BMS_4130)
bms_4130_08004410.description: Per-tick estimator for the value at status +0x128. The status object comes from the BMS_4130 accessor (bms_ram_20000bdc_addr in this build), and bit 2 of its u16 at +0x124 gates everything. While the bit is set it samples the s16 at +0x11A into 0x20000116 when the value is 1 to 1399, and after ten counts latches it into 0x20000114. The estimate is ((u16 +0x104 x DAT_20000CDC / 100) - (DAT_20000D94 x 0x50 + DAT_20000D90 x 0x14) / 100) x 1000 / reference x 60 / 10000, with 30 added when +0x104 exceeds 95. Above 0x1503 on +0x118 the estimate loses one unit every 600 ticks, and a hold in 0x20000118 with a switch-over rule decides what reaches +0x128, which is written only inside range checks (499). When the gate bit is clear the holds are reset.
bms_4130_08004410.notes: The x60 and /10000 scaling suggests minutes, which is an inference. The reference 0x20000116 and the RAM terms 0x20000CDC, 0x20000D90 and 0x20000D94 are not identified in this packet. Helper bms_4168_0800113c is not yet described.

bms_4168_08004488.name: bms_profile_table_fill_4168
bms_4168_08004488.summary: Fill the 4168 record table and threshold bytes for profile id 0x20000024
bms_4168_08004488.description: Fills 20 records through bms_record12_addr for the 4168 build (accessor FUN_0800CE3C). The record at index 1 takes 0x35 for id 5 and 0x2D otherwise, and record 2 takes 0xFD2 for id 5 and 0x1036 otherwise; record 0x12 copies +0x86 and +0x88, records 0x2C, 0x2B and 0x31 are derived from the status block (0x2C from +0x6C, 0x2B and 0x31 from +0x70), and the rest are fixed pairs. The profile id at DAT_20000024 sets +0x86 and +0x88 (0x35 and 0x30 for ids 6 to 8, 0x3A and 0x35 otherwise) and +0x192 (0x17C for id 5, 400 otherwise), and +0x6C, +0x70 and +0x76 by group: (4-5), (3, 6, 8), (2, 7), (0) and other. The routine only writes records and status fields.
bms_4168_08004488.notes: Sibling of bms_profile_table_fill_4139 and bms_profile_table_fill_4130 with a different id mapping and record set. The purpose of each record is not stated in the packet.

bms_4139_08004618.name: bms_remaining_time_4139
bms_4139_08004618.summary: Update the minutes-like estimate at status +0x128 with hold and hysteresis (BMS_4139)
bms_4139_08004618.description: Estimator of the same family as bms_remaining_time_4130 for BMS_4139, using the RAM terms DAT_20000D38, DAT_20000DEC and DAT_20000DF0 and the reference DAT_20000158. Bit 2 of the u16 at +0x124 gates it: when set it samples the s16 at +0x11A into the holds at 0x20000156..0x2000015C, latching after ten counts, and when clear it resets the holds. The estimate is ((u16 +0x104 x DAT_20000D38 / 100) - (DAT_20000DF0 x 0x50 + DAT_20000DEC x 0x14) / 100) x 1000 / reference x 60 / 10000, clamped at zero. A one-shot flag at 0x2000014C enables a band correction on +0x118 above 0x1503, and a count of 599 steps lowers the held value by one. The result is written to +0x128 inside a range check of 499.
bms_4139_08004618.notes: The minutes reading and the meaning of the RAM terms are inferences, as for bms_remaining_time_4130. Helper bms_4168_0800113c is not yet described.

bms_4168_08004de8.name: bms_comm_request_dispatch
bms_4168_08004de8.summary: Pick the next queued link request (0x16, 0x1E, 0x18) and send it, else count the queue down
bms_4168_08004de8.description: Part of the host-link request layer, with bms_comm_send_frame, bms_comm_req_cmd02/04/06 and bms_comm_await_reply_cmd03. When the pending-count byte at +0x101 is zero it sets the state byte at +0xF9 to 9 and returns. Otherwise it bumps the retry byte at +0xFB, zeroes the reply timer word at +0x00 and checks three request flags in order: +0xFC sends command 0x16 with no payload, +0xFE sends command 0x1E with one payload word (the byte at +0xFF, also stored at +0x3C), and +0xFD sends command 0x18 with no payload. Each send sets state +0xF9 to 0x0C. With no request pending it decrements the count at +0x101 and returns.

params.name: unused
params.description: param_1; not read by the routine

params.name: ctx
params.description: param_2; link context: state +0xF9, retry +0xFB, timer +0x00, flags +0xFC..+0xFE, count +0x101

bms_4168_08004de8.notes: Command meanings 0x16, 0x18 and 0x1E are not identified in the packet. The state values 9 and 0x0C are the ones this function sets.

bms_4168_08004fec.name: bms_auth_verify_response
bms_4168_08004fec.summary: Check a 16-byte reply (cmd 0x1D, type 4) against a value computed from the object at 0x20000BCC
bms_4168_08004fec.description: Timer-driven check of a challenge reply in the host-link layer. param_1 (elapsed time) is added to the reply timer at +0x00 of the context; past 200 the state at +0xF9 becomes 5 (retry) while fewer than four retries have been used, and 0x0D (fault) otherwise. When a frame is pending (flag 0x200001AD) and its header is command 0x1D with type nibble 4, the four 32-bit words at 0x2000092C..0x2000093B are gathered and bms_4168_080106c8 (not described) computes a 16-byte value from the object at 0x20000BCC. That value is repacked into four 32-bit words and compared with the reply. A match clears the retry byte at +0xFB and sets state +0xF9 to 7. The pending flag is cleared on every pass.

params.name: elapsed
params.description: param_1; time added to the reply timer

params.name: ctx
params.description: param_2; link context with state +0xF9, retry +0xFB and timer +0x00

bms_4168_08004fec.notes: This is the authentication core of the link, and the algorithm in bms_4168_080106c8 is not in this packet, so the nature of the 16-byte value (MAC, cipher output or hash) is unknown. The byte-swap repacking is decompiled awkwardly and should be checked against the source.

bms_4168_08005128.name: bms_comm_send_frame
bms_4168_08005128.summary: Build and send a framed message on USART3: magic, command, count and sequence, payload, CRC-16
bms_4168_08005128.description: Builds the outgoing host-link frame and sends it with bms_usart3_send_bytes. Byte 0 is a magic, 0x5A when DAT_200001AE is 1 and 0xA5 otherwise. Byte 1 is the command (the low byte of param_1). Byte 2 holds the payload word count in its high nibble and the 4-bit sequence number from the context at +0xFA in its low nibble. Then come param_3 payload words, each sent big-endian, then the CRC-16/USB (bms_4168_08004da4) over bytes 1 to the end of the payload, high byte first. The sequence number at +0xFA advances mod 8 after each frame. The header and payload are also mirrored into globals 0x20000904 to 0x2000090E (payload stored little-endian there), with the CRC bytes at 0x20000927-0x20000928.

params.name: cmd
params.description: param_1; command code, used as its low byte

params.name: words
params.description: param_2; payload array of 32-bit words

params.name: count
params.description: param_3; number of payload words

params.name: ctx
params.description: param_4; link context whose +0xFA byte holds the sequence number

bms_4168_08005128.notes: Frame layout is read from the stores and the CRC length (count x 4 + 2). The CRC algorithm is in the wave-1 summary of bms_4168_08004da4. The receive side of the same protocol is in bms_proto_build_reply and bms_auth_verify_response.

bms_4168_08005228.name: bms_comm_req_cmd02
bms_4168_08005228.summary: Send command 0x02 with no payload, reset the reply timer, and enter state 2
bms_4168_08005228.description: Request step of the host-link layer. It increments the request counter at +0xFB, zeroes the reply timer at +0x00, sends command 0x02 with no payload through bms_comm_send_frame, and sets the state byte at +0xF9 to 2. The reply is collected by bms_comm_await_reply_cmd03 and timed through the reply timer.

params.name: unused
params.description: param_1; not read by the routine

params.name: ctx
params.description: param_2; link context

bms_4168_08005228.notes: The meaning of command 0x02 is not in the packet.

bms_4168_0800525c.name: bms_comm_await_reply_cmd03
bms_4168_0800525c.summary: Wait for the command-03 reply: accept into ctx+0x08, retry after 200 ticks, fault after 11 retries
bms_4168_0800525c.description: Timer step of the host-link layer for requests such as bms_comm_req_cmd02. It adds param_1 to the reply timer at +0x00; past 200 it sets state +0xF9 to 1 (retry) while the retry byte at +0xFB is below 11, and to 0x0D (fault) otherwise. When a frame is pending (flag 0x200001AD) whose header byte at 0x2000092A is 3 and whose high nibble at 0x2000092B is 1, it stores the four payload bytes at 0x2000092C as a little-endian word into ctx+0x08, clears the retry byte, sets state +0xF9 to 3 (reply received), and sets bit 4 of the u16 at +0x194 of the status object from the 0x20000BDC accessor. The pending flag is cleared on every pass.

params.name: elapsed
params.description: param_1; time added to the reply timer

params.name: ctx
params.description: param_2; link context with reply word at +0x08, state +0xF9, retry +0xFB

bms_4168_0800525c.notes: The state values 1 and 3 are only set here, and the packet does not show what the caller does with them.

bms_4168_080052e0.name: bms_comm_req_cmd06
bms_4168_080052e0.summary: Send command 0x06 with no payload, reset the reply timer, and enter state 8
bms_4168_080052e0.description: Request step of the host-link layer, the same shape as bms_comm_req_cmd02: it increments the request counter at +0xFB, zeroes the reply timer at +0x00, sends command 0x06 with no payload through bms_comm_send_frame and sets the state byte at +0xF9 to 8.
